slides.heading: What is Python?
slides.body: What is Python? is part of Introduction to Python and Output. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: What is Python?
slides.body: Python is a beginner-friendly programming language used to give instructions to a computer. In this lesson, you will see how a simple line of Python can produce visible output on the screen.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Think of Python like a clear recipe card. Each line is an instruction, and the computer follows the recipe exactly as written.

annotations.note: This line displays a value or message on the screen.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Write one clear instruction at a time. Python reads your code from top to bottom, so order and spelling matter.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Use print() to display your own name on the screen.
slides.hint: Type print("Your Name") and replace the words inside the quotes.

quiz.prompt_text: What is Python best described as?

options: A beginner-friendly programming language used to give instructions to a computer
A web browser for viewing websites
A database for storing large files

quiz.explanation: Correct! Python is a beginner-friendly programming language. You use it to write instructions that tell the computer what to do.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines of code in the correct order to display 'Hello, World!' on the screen.
quiz.explanation: The comment comes first to explain the code, then the print() call runs to show the message, and the closing comment goes last.

quiz.prompt_text: Write a short program that prints your own name on the screen using print().

content.hint: Type print("Your Name") and replace the words inside the quotes with your actual name.

quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: Use print("Your Name") — replace 'Your Name' with any text. Python will display whatever is inside the quotation marks.
